title: Tensei shitara Slime Datta Ken Movie 2: Soukai no Namida-hen
content:
Can I say something controversial? The fact that this movie was better than season 3 of the anime says so little about it and so much about that season. Even though it took Fuse overseeing the production, unlike the first movie, it paled in comparison regarding a few areas.

Let’s praise what deserves to be praised first. For what I think is the first time in this franchise that the main focus was not Rimuru, the fact that they put the spotlights on Gobta of all characters says a lot about the confidence the writers placed on the plot and conflict of this movie alone. Theywere sure it stood firmly on its own that using one of the more unsafe characters would not be a problem, and I would say that they were right in their bet.

Some would say that the fact that they picked Gobta at all was not really unsafe and was even the right call. But there are a lot of opinions regarding this. Being the underdog he was always established to be, this movie gives Gobta the time to shine before we end up seeing less of him as he takes off to train with Millim at the end of season 3, so it tracks.

It might just be me, but it felt weird that I thought the animation and production quality overall was weaker than that of movie one. Nothing was subpar or anything, but it felt unnoticed, no moment really gripped and had you acknowledge anything worthy of praise in that department. The same can be said about voice acting and SFX. Is that goblin racism I’m sensing?

All in all, it did not feel like a memorable movie unfortunately. The villains were bland, the vacation mission is already a tired concept, and too many characters were involved for such a short conflict that it felt like it took more screen time from Gobta and Yura. Speaking of which, Yura’s design might be the only memorable thing about the entire movie, or rather, the gradient choice on her hair.

Overall: 6.66/10.
